COVID-19 will weigh on activity and pose near-term risks, but the Fed’s rapid move to the effective lower bound, large-scale purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS, expanded repos, discount-window easing, and coordinated dollar swap lines is consistent with countercyclical policy and the credit-channel literature. Evidence from Oliner and Rudebusch (1996a), Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein (1994), and Gertler and Gilchrist (1994) indicates that policies which support bank balance sheets and market functioning lower external finance premia, helping stabilize investment and employment. With muted inflation pressures and falling market-based inflation compensation, the stance aligns with inflation-forecast-targeting principles (Svensson) and reinforces credibility around a symmetric 2 percent objective, addressing time-inconsistency concerns. Given liquidity-trap risk at near-zero rates, balance-sheet tools and swap lines help prevent a sharper deterioration in credit conditions and international dollar funding. Net: the outlook is negative, but decisive policy materially mitigates downside risks.
